messages:
sam: Heads-up — nightly CI bench flagged ~9% p99 latency regression for kernel-v2 on ada-quant when replaying last week's prod traces. @anya @mike can you take a look? :eyes:
anya: Which harness did the job use — replay or synthetic?
sam: Replay harness, seed=prod-2026-03-12. Job id = `ci/bench/nightly/bench-2026-03-12-07`. Config: `batch_target=8`, `max_seq=1024`, `kv_cache=enabled`, `kernel_policy=auto`.
mike: Got it. Can you paste the profiler summary (hotspots, memcpy vs compute)?
sam: Summary from `perf-summary.json` small excerpt:
```
kernel_selector: fallback_count=132 out_of=910
attention_time: +14.8% vs baseline
matmul_time: +3.2% vs baseline
memcpy_time: +22% (more small memcpy calls)
```
Looks like more small-batch traffic triggered fallback kernels a lot.
perf-bot: [alert] nightly-bench latency/p99 breach (9%). Created perf-alert-4587. Link: https://redwood.internal/alerts/4587 :rotating_light:
anya: If fallback kernels are spiking, the selector heuristics probably mis-classified small micro-batches. Did the replay change traffic shape?
sam: Replay used the same trace but we updated the harness to not coalesce near-empty requests; so more micro-batches showed up. Might be harness config drift.
mike: Reproduced locally with the replay harness. Kernel selector logs show threshold 'min_batch_for_fastpath' lowered accidentally in the last config PR.
julie: Can we run a synthetic apples-to-apples run (same seq distribution but with controlled inter-arrival) to confirm it's selector vs model perf? I'll kick one.
ci-bot: Starting job `ci/bench/synth/compare-179876` (synth harness, preserved seq histogram), ETA ~12m.
ci-bot: Job `ci/bench/synth/compare-179876` finished. Results attached.
anya: Synthetic run shows p99 stable (within 1%) but replay still +8-9%. That points at batching/coalescing differences rather than kernel perf.
mike: Agreed. Short-term mitigation: raise `min_batch_for_fastpath` from 2->4 for kernel-v2 and enable aggressive coalescing in the replay harness. I'll open a tiny deploy.
sam: Also let's add a KV-cache warmup step in the harness (warm prefix of 64 tokens) — profiler showed tmphit penalty on first real request.
julie: For CI automation: do we want this to create a flaky-alert if variance >3% across 3 runs, or auto-suppress until config drift is resolved?
anya: Let's follow triage flow: rerun replay 3x, if >=2 runs show >6% regress -> create perf-alert (keep current). If results are mixed, mark flaky and add to flaky-dashboard for manual review.
mike: I'll push the selector patch + harness coalescing within the hour. Also adding a small unit test that asserts `kernel_selector.fallback_rate < 0.05` on a synthetic micro-batch workload.
sam: Cool. Please link the PR here and tag `perf-review` label. I'll update the dashboard: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/bench/perf-alert-4587 with before/after plots.
julie: Quick note for CI: publish both replay and synth results to the same dashboard panel for apples-to-apples comparison and enable an annotation if harness config changed in the last 24h.
anm: (typo)
perf-bot: perf-alert-4587 status -> triage_in_progress.
mike: PR #3241 opened: `runtime: tighten selector thresholds for kernel-v2` — includes tests and changelog.
sam: Thanks everyone. Action items: mike (patch + tests), anya (update triage rule docs), julie (dashboard annotation), sam (open follow-up to add KV warmup to all replay jobs). We'll rerun nightly after deploy and re-evaluate. :white_check_mark:
